answer: Proof-of-spacetime mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to cryptographically demonstrate persistent allocation of unique hard-drive sectors. The registry acts as a haven against sybil swarms, forcing an adversary to incur the verifiable hardware cost of dedicating physical storage per identity. Even at the zenith of media density, an attacker cannot harbor phantom instances without real disk capacity. However, this design inherently disadvantages storage-constrained edge agents.
